title: Best Sandals (2026)
summary: A guide to the top sandals for 2026 based on multiple expert reviews.
method: Picks were chosen from The Inertia, OutdoorGearLab, and CleverHiker articles, favoring models cited by more than one source.
assumptions: Prices are taken as listed in the sources; no price comparisons were made beyond what was provided.

products.name: Chaco Z/1 Classic
why: The Inertia calls it the top overall pick for its comfort and support. CleverHiker lists it as a stable and durable hiking sandal.
It has a supportive footbed, adjustable straps, and a sturdy sole that handles creek crossings and long hikes.
products.desc: A sandal with a cushy footbed, adjustable straps, and a sturdy sole. It does not have a low profile and can feel heavy.
products.benefit: Picture a day hike where you cross streams and need secure footing. The Chaco gives you adjustable support and a molded footbed that stays comfortable all day. It beats the other picks by being the only sandal noted for both high support and durability across multiple guides. The catch: its high profile makes it feel heavier than lighter options.

products.name: Birkenstock Arizona Soft Footbed
why: OutdoorGearLab names it the best everyday sandal for its classic style and footbed that molds over time.
It offers casual style, comfort, and support for long days on the go.
products.desc: A two‑strap sandal with a cork footbed that molds to the foot. It is not water‑friendly.
products.benefit: Picture a city stroll where you need a sandal that’s easy to slip on and stays comfortable all day. The Birkenstock provides a moldable cork footbed and simple strap design, giving it the most reliable everyday comfort among the picks. It wins over Chaco for casual wear and over Teva for style, but it lacks water friendliness. The catch: it is not suited for wet conditions.

products.name: Teva Original Universal
why: Both The Inertia and OutdoorGearLab list it as the best value sandal for its lightweight, water‑friendly design.
It comes in many colors and is easy to pack for travel.
products.desc: A lightweight sandal with a simple strap system and water‑friendly sole. It does not have a molded footbed.
products.benefit: Picture a beach day where you need a sandal that dries quickly and fits in a bag. The Teva offers lightweight comfort and water resistance, making it the most travel‑ready option here. It beats the Birkenstock on water use and is cheaper than the Chaco, though it lacks the same level of support. The catch: it lacks a molded footbed for extra cushioning.

verdict.line: Buy it if you need supportive, stable sandals for active use like hiking or creek crossings. It offers a molded footbed and adjustable straps, but its high profile can feel heavy.
